html:
The Somavamshis ruled parts of today's Odisha and Chhattisgarh from about the 9th century to the early 12th. On the 900 map they hold the hills and coast south of Bengal.

They began in Dakshina Kosala, the upper Mahanadi valley, and later took over the Odisha coast after the Bhauma-Kara dynasty. Their kings, such as Yayati I, ruled from Yayatinagara and other cities, and were great temple builders. Odisha's temple style took its classic form under them, with the Mukteshvara temple and the great Lingaraja Temple at Bhubaneswar.

In the early 1100s the Eastern Gangas under Anantavarman Chodaganga took their lands. The Gangas went on to build the Jagannath temple at Puri and the Konark Sun Temple. See also Orissa and Kalinga.
